title: Post-symptomatic restoration of severe genetic neurodevelopmental disorders

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a treatment that restores deficient gene function after a severe genetic neurodevelopmental disorder has become clinically established, substantially reverses existing impairments, and enables sustained developmental progress. The goal extends beyond improving a symptom score: children would recover or acquire meaningful communication, purposeful hand use, mobility and other abilities that their disorder had prevented or disrupted. Restoration to age-typical function remains an additional, more demanding ambition.

Angelman syndrome and Rett syndrome provide specific molecular routes toward this goal. Rugonersen is an antisense oligonucleotide intended to restore UBE3A expression in Angelman syndrome by releasing the normally silenced paternal allele. TSHA-102 is a MECP2-directed gene therapy intended to optimize expression in the central nervous system in Rett syndrome. These approaches supply a technical basis for attempting restoration after symptoms emerge, but their reported biological and functional signals do not establish the full proposed capability.

significance.text: As a conditional assessment, substantially reversing established developmental impairments through restoration of deficient gene function would establish a major therapeutic capability. Achieving age-typical communication, motor function and cognitive attainment after an established phenotype would be an even stronger result. The direct benefit would concern the children, treatment ages and particular disorder actually studied; it would not automatically establish restoration across severe genetic neurodevelopmental disorders.

The distinction between developmental progress and developmental catch-up is essential. A child may acquire important milestones and subsequently learn at a rate overlapping typically developing children while retaining a substantial gap in age-expected abilities. Such progress could be highly meaningful without demonstrating age-typical attainment. Similarly, improvements in communication or motor function cannot alone establish cognitive recovery. The TANGELO supplementary analyses reinforce the need to distinguish group-level score changes from changes that are meaningful for an individual child.

As a conditional downstream possibility, success could motivate analogous treatments for other disorders with tractable molecular causes and investigation of restoration at later ages. Each extension would require evidence about its own disease mechanism, treatment distribution, expression requirements and capacity for functional recovery. Benefit in adults with longstanding impairments, or extension to idiopathic autism, is not established by the supplied evidence. The significance of this innovation does not depend on asserting a historical consensus that established developmental impairments were universally irreversible.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability in the supplied evidence is reliable, substantial functional restoration after symptoms are established. Molecular intervention must lead to meaningful recovery and sustained learning, rather than only a change in an EEG measure, a severity score or a small set of milestones. The available Angelman and Rett reports provide evidence of partial biological or functional responses, but do not demonstrate the proposed breadth of restoration.

Candidate engineering barriers include reaching the relevant neurons across affected brain regions, producing sufficient gene function in those cells and maintaining safe expression over time. Viral-vector dose constraints may matter for gene-transfer approaches, while drug exposure and distribution require separate assessment for an antisense approach. These are proposed barriers for this concept, not a combination of established limitations demonstrated by the supplied sources. In particular, the TANGELO supplement states that its pharmacokinetic data could not establish brain drug concentrations; that measurement limitation does not by itself demonstrate failed brain-wide delivery or a viral-vector dose ceiling.

A further proposed scientific barrier is whether affected circuits retain, or can recover, the capacity to support learning after prolonged deficient gene function. Restoring expression may be necessary without being sufficient to rebuild useful function. Treatment-age effects, reversibility of different impairments and the contribution of rehabilitation would therefore need direct investigation. The supplied evidence does not resolve these questions or establish that a particular developmental window has permanently closed.

current_state.text: Hipp, Bacino, Bird and colleagues reported the phase 1 TANGELO trial of rugonersen in Nature Medicine on 11 July 2025, DOI 10.1038/s41591-025-03784-7. The abstract retained in the supplied review describes an open-label trial involving 61 children aged 1–12 years with Angelman syndrome. The primary safety and tolerability endpoint was met. Exploratory analyses indicated a dose-related movement of the syndrome-associated EEG abnormality toward normal and clinical improvement signals exceeding natural-history expectations. These findings support further investigation, but do not establish substantial developmental restoration or age-typical function. The article's statement that Angelman syndrome lacked disease-modifying treatment describes the situation at publication, not a verified approval status as of November 2026.

The available TANGELO material has important limits. The supplied review had access to the article's abstract through a subscription preview and to complete supplementary information, rather than the main article body and original figures. The supplement discusses limitations of external natural-history comparisons and of estimates of clinical meaningfulness. Because suitable anchor-based data were insufficient, some meaningful-change estimates relied on score distributions and reliability. Domain-specific changes relative to natural history therefore require cautious interpretation and do not establish age-typical development. A second associated PDF yielded essentially no extractable text, and its identity could not be confirmed from its contents; no substantive conclusion here depends on it.

For Rett syndrome, a NeurologyLive report dated 15 October 2026 summarizes a conference presentation about TSHA-102 using a May 2025 data cutoff. It reports that all ten REVEAL Part A participants gained or regained at least one developmental milestone after a single intrathecal dose. Reported gains included communication abilities, purposeful hand use and finger feeding. Participants described in the report were aged 6–21 years. The account concerns open-label studies using external natural-history comparisons, without a concurrent control arm. It is a conference-based secondary report with sponsor involvement; the underlying trial report was not available in the supplied review. The reported milestone gains do not demonstrate typical development.

The research notes also attribute an NGN-401 update to a Neurogene company release dated 27 October 2026: ten participants at a 16 June 2026 cutoff, with continued milestone acquisition over follow-up extending to 30 months. Those details remain unverified within the supplied record because no release text was retained for review. They should be treated as an attributed sponsor report requiring confirmation, rather than as established trial findings. The absence of retained evidence does not show that the reported result is false.

Taken together, the supplied evidence documents exploratory biological and functional signals in molecularly targeted treatment programs. It does not demonstrate the proposed post-symptomatic restoration to age-typical development. This conclusion is bounded by the supplied reports: no freshness search record was provided, so the record cannot establish a comprehensive field-wide treatment or achievement status as of 1 November 2026.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: children with genetically confirmed Angelman syndrome or Rett syndrome would receive treatment after documented skill loss or a clear developmental plateau. Where absent at baseline, they would acquire functional speech or a prespecified equivalent level of communication, purposeful hand use and independent walking. They would sustain skill acquisition for at least two years at rates overlapping prespecified typically developing reference groups. These milestones and the two-year duration are proposed criteria for this innovation, not established clinical standards.
completion_criteria.label: Functional restoration and typical-rate skill acquisition sustained for two years

completion_criteria.text: A convincing study would prespecify baseline abilities, treatment ages, outcome measures, responder thresholds, the meaning of equivalent communication and the reference ages used to judge developmental rates. Natural-history comparisons would be specified in advance, with their limitations addressed; concurrent controls and blinded outcome assessment should be used where feasible. The demonstration would need to establish meaningful individual functional change as well as group effects. A few milestone gains accompanied by persistent severe disability would fall short of this proposal, even if those gains were clinically valuable.
completion_criteria.label: Prespecified comparisons demonstrate meaningful individual functional change and group effects

completion_criteria.text: Meeting the functional and developmental-rate criteria would demonstrate substantial restoration and sustained progress. A stronger claim of age-typical development would additionally require age-normed evidence across communication, motor and cognitive domains, showing attained abilities rather than only learning velocity. Proposed confirmation would include reproducibility across independent cohorts or sites, durable benefit, acceptable safety and clear reporting of nonresponders and treatment burden. Finite studies would establish demonstrated breadth within the tested disorders, ages, genotypes and baseline impairments; they would not establish universal reversibility or justify extrapolation to adults.
completion_criteria.label: Stronger: Age-normed evidence demonstrates age-typical communication, motor and cognitive abilities

related_concepts.text: Roster-based conceptual comparison: PED-06, Prenatal correction that lets severe monogenic disease develop normally, and PED-11, One-time in vivo correction of severe newborn metabolic disease before irreversible injury, share the use of molecular treatment to alter a disease's developmental consequences. Their defining timing and outcomes differ from PED-09: PED-06 seeks normal development through prenatal correction, and PED-11 emphasizes correction before irreversible injury. PED-09 requires recovery after a neurodevelopmental phenotype is established. Prevention and post-symptomatic restoration remain separate capabilities.

Roster-based conceptual comparison: PED-04, Controlled reopening of developmental critical periods, overlaps with the question of whether established circuits can regain developmental competence. Its focus is control of plasticity, whereas PED-09 centers on restoring deficient gene function in a defined disorder. A plasticity intervention could hypothetically complement molecular restoration, but neither capability demonstrates the other, and the supplied material does not establish that reopening a critical period is necessary for PED-09.

Roster-based conceptual comparison: PED-03, Reversal of established childhood stunting and its cognitive cost, shares the ambition of recovery after a developmental deficit has emerged, but addresses a different causal setting. PED-05, Prevention of cerebral palsy after perinatal brain injury, concerns prevention of a neurological outcome after injury rather than reversal of an established genetic phenotype. PED-08, Restoration of nephron endowment after the nephrogenic clock stops, shares the broader question of recovery beyond a developmental window while targeting a different organ and biological process. These comparisons use the supplied roster titles; fuller specifications were not available to establish more detailed overlap.

change_log.reason: Learning at a typical rate after a delay does not itself close an existing developmental gap or establish recovery across unmeasured domains.

change_log.change: Removed the asserted historical consensus of irreversibility and the generalization about usual diagnostic timing.
change_log.reason: The supplied evidence does not establish those factual premises, and the conditional significance of the concept does not depend on them.

change_log.reason: The retained texts do not substantiate the full set as established barriers; uncertain brain exposure is narrower than demonstrated delivery failure.

change_log.reason: These distinctions determine how strongly the reported safety, biological and clinical findings can be interpreted.

change_log.reason: The dated report supports reported functional gains, not a peer-reviewed demonstration of typical development.

unresolved_issues: The NGN-401 release text is absent. Its stated publication date, participant count, data cutoff, follow-up duration and milestone findings remain unverified within this record.
The main TANGELO article body and original figures were not available to the supplied review. A second associated PDF lacked usable extracted text and content-confirmed identity.
No freshness search record establishes comprehensive achievement or approval status as of 1 November 2026.
The relative importance of brain distribution, safe expression, viral-vector dose constraints and circuit competence requires direct evidence for each treatment and disorder.
Communication equivalence, reference ages, responder thresholds and acceptable safety and treatment burden remain to be operationalized for the proposed demonstration.
The extent to which benefits reproduce across ages, genotypes and baseline impairments, or extend to adults and other disorders, remains unresolved.

The review recommended withholding the unverified NGN-401 figures from the evidentiary account. They were retained only as explicitly qualified research-note attributions to preserve potentially useful quantitative detail without treating it as confirmed.
Detailed overlap with other roster entries cannot be resolved from titles alone; the related-concept comparisons are limited accordingly.

brief.title: Restoring development after genetic disorders
possible: Children whose genetic disorders have disrupted development could regain lost abilities or acquire skills they never developed. Treatment would restore deficient gene function after symptoms appear, helping them communicate, use their hands purposefully and move independently.
The goal is substantial recovery followed by sustained learning. Angelman and Rett syndromes, genetic conditions that severely disrupt development, offer specific starting points.
why: For affected children, recovery would mean practical abilities: expressing needs, feeding themselves and walking. Treatment could change their developmental path after difficulties are already established.
Success could also motivate treatments for other disorders with identifiable genetic causes and research into recovery at later ages.

sources.who: Jörg F. Hipp, Carlos A. Bacino, Lynne M. Bird and colleagues
sources.showed: Rugonersen, a drug designed to restore deficient gene activity in Angelman syndrome, met the trial's safety goal. Exploratory results showed brain electrical activity moving toward normal and signs of functional improvement.
sources.quote: The primary endpoint was met; rugonersen had an acceptable safety and tolerability profile.
sources.cited_for: The trial supports attempting recovery by restoring gene function after symptoms appear.
sources.not_established: A trial without a concurrent control group cannot establish substantial recovery from these exploratory changes.

sources.showed: This is a company update about developmental milestone acquisition during treatment.
sources.cited_for: It describes another treatment program reporting developmental gains.
sources.not_established: A sponsor report of milestone gains does not establish broad, sustained functional recovery.

sources.who: Elsa Rossignol and REVEAL collaborators, including Taysha Gene Therapies
sources.showed: A conference report described gains in communication, hand use and mobility after gene therapy, a treatment intended to restore gene function. The small Rett syndrome studies had no concurrent control group and included sponsor involvement.
sources.quote: Communication gains included use of phrases and improved communication, while fine motor gains included purposeful hand use and finger feeding.
sources.cited_for: The reported gains support the possibility of acquiring or recovering skills after established impairment.
sources.not_established: These gains do not establish broad recovery or abilities typical for a person's age.

shown: Hipp and colleagues tested rugonersen in 61 children with Angelman syndrome. Their strongest findings combine acceptable safety with preliminary biological and functional responses.
Rossignol and colleagues reported that all ten participants receiving the Rett syndrome treatment gained or regained a developmental milestone. These are early signs of recovery.
missing: Treatment must reliably produce substantial recovery across everyday abilities after symptoms are established.
Recovered abilities must support sustained learning at rates comparable to typical development.
Benefits must last with acceptable safety and repeat across independent groups.

milestones.label: Functional recovery and typical learning rates sustained for two years
milestones.explanation: After skill loss or a plateau, children would gain missing speech or equivalent communication, purposeful hand use and independent walking, then sustain typical learning rates for two years. This would establish recovery and continued progress.

milestones.label: Planned comparisons establish meaningful individual and group gains
milestones.explanation: Studies would define meaningful gains and comparisons in advance, accounting for starting abilities and treatment ages, with controls and blinded assessments where feasible. This would establish benefits for individuals and groups.

milestones.label: Stronger evidence establishes abilities typical for age
milestones.explanation: Age-based tests would show typical communication, movement and thinking abilities, with lasting, acceptably safe benefits reproduced independently. This would establish developmental catch-up beyond faster learning.

uncertain: It remains unclear how much recovery depends on treatment age, starting abilities and rehabilitation.
The gene activity needed across brain regions, and the ability of affected brain circuits to recover, remain unresolved.
Equivalent communication, meaningful improvement thresholds and acceptable treatment burdens still need clear definitions.

page.title: Post-symptomatic gene restoration in Angelman and Rett syndromes
page.definition: After symptoms appear, treatment restores UBE3A function in neurons in Angelman syndrome or MECP2 function in neurons in Rett syndrome, enabling a person to acquire or regain developmental skills. Approaches include supplying a functional copy of the affected gene and, in Angelman syndrome, turning on the normally silent UBE3A copy inherited from the father.

goal.need: In Angelman syndrome, the estimated chance of brushing teeth with help by age 15 was 13% with a class I deletion and 85% with a pathogenic UBE3A variant. Among 1,228 females with classic Rett syndrome, fewer than 6.3% of eligible participants gained or regained any of 51 skills per year after age six. Therapies teach skills and medicines ease symptoms, but the protein deficiency persists. Gaining hand use or communication after symptoms appear could reduce dependence in daily life. Recovery may vary by skill, as it does in Angelman mouse models.

figures.caption: Angelman syndrome: skills with at least 50% acquisition probability by age 15.
figures.note: Natural-history cohort: 261 participants. These are counts of skills meeting a model-estimated probability threshold, not average skills acquired per participant.

completion.title: FDA approves a gene-restoring treatment that improves development after symptom onset.
completion.criterion: For each syndrome separately, FDA grants marketing approval to a treatment that restores deficient UBE3A or MECP2 function in patients with established symptoms, with the efficacy determination based on acquired or recovered developmental abilities. The approved population and demonstrated follow-up define the scope of achievement.
completion.set_by: Atlas operational criterion combining FDA marketing approval with developmental-function benefit.
completion.basis: FDA determines safety and effectiveness for the proposed indication. The Atlas requires evidence that gene restoration enables patients with established symptoms to acquire or regain developmental abilities. For example, FDA approved trofinetide for Rett syndrome on caregiver symptom ratings and clinician ratings of overall improvement at 12 weeks. That approval establishes a different benefit. Developmental gains apply to the population and follow-up studied.

milestones.title: Gene restoration produces the expected biological response in an animal with established disease signs.
milestones.criterion: A relevant animal model shows signs of the disorder before gene restoration. After intervention, the model shows a biological response consistent with the response expected in humans.
milestones.set_by: FDA, Human Gene Therapy for Rare Diseases, section IV, recommends the model-response test for gene-therapy products. The post-onset condition defines the scope of this entry.
milestones.threshold_quote: should demonstrate a biological response to the investigational GT product that is similar to the expected response in humans.

milestones.title: A symptomatic patient receives a gene-restoring treatment in an early-phase clinical trial.
milestones.criterion: At least one participant with established symptoms receives the investigational UBE3A- or MECP2-restoring treatment under an early-phase clinical protocol.
milestones.set_by: FDA, 21 CFR 312.21(a), defines initial human administration. TANGELO and the early REVEAL cohorts apply this stage to the two syndromes.
milestones.threshold_quote: initial introduction of an investigational new drug into humans.

milestones.title: A symptomatic patient receives a gene-restoring treatment in a pivotal efficacy trial.
milestones.criterion: At least one symptomatic participant receives the gene-restoring treatment in the pivotal cohort of a study designed to evaluate efficacy and safety for a marketing application. In a multiphase protocol, the qualifying dose must be given in the pivotal part.
milestones.set_by: FDA, 21 CFR 312.21(c), defines phase 3; the BEACON, pivotal REVEAL and Embolden protocols implement the pivotal efficacy stage for these syndromes.
milestones.threshold_quote: Phase 3 studies are expanded controlled and uncontrolled trials.

milestones.title: A gene-restoring treatment meets its pivotal developmental-function efficacy endpoint.
milestones.criterion: Meet the trial's prespecified primary developmental endpoint. In Rett syndrome at 12 months, Embolden requires at least 9 of 25 participants both to gain at least one of 28 milestones and to score 3 or better on the Clinical Global Impression of Improvement. TSHA-102 REVEAL requires at least 33% to gain or regain at least one of 28 milestones. In Angelman syndrome, BEACON compares change in Bayley-4 raw cognition or expressive communication with sham at week 56 in ages 1–17. Obudanersen REVEAL compares change in raw expressive communication without caregiver input with placebo at week 52 in its paediatric cohort. ASPIRE compares change in raw cognition with sham at week 48.
milestones.set_by: The Embolden and TSHA-102 REVEAL protocols define separate Rett responder thresholds. Oak Hill Bio, Ionis and Ultragenyx define the Angelman endpoints for BEACON, obudanersen REVEAL and ASPIRE respectively. The quoted threshold is specific to TSHA-102 REVEAL.
milestones.threshold_quote: A response rate of 33% is the minimum threshold for success sufficient to reject the natural history established null hypothesis of 6.7%

milestones.title: An early clinical study finds preliminary evidence of improved developmental function.
milestones.criterion: An early clinical study in symptomatic participants reports improvement on a developmental assessment after gene restoration, using the study's baseline, natural-history comparison or concurrent control. The assessment must measure an ability such as communication, hand use or mobility.
milestones.set_by: FDA, 21 CFR 312.21(c), describes preliminary evidence before phase 3. TANGELO and the early Rett studies specify the functional assessments.
milestones.threshold_quote: preliminary evidence suggesting effectiveness of the drug has been obtained

milestones.title: FDA accepts a marketing application for a gene-restoring treatment for substantive review.
milestones.criterion: FDA notifies the applicant that it has filed the new drug application or biologics license application for review. The application seeks an indication in symptomatic patients with Angelman or Rett syndrome and includes evidence on acquisition or recovery of developmental abilities.
milestones.set_by: FDA, new drug and biologics license application review process, and Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research, SOPP 8401, definition of a filing letter.
milestones.threshold_quote: A letter issued to notify the applicant that their submission has been filed and will be reviewed.

not_found: BEACON's public documents did not disclose a statistical success cutoff or an individual meaningful-change threshold.
ClinicalTrials.gov records for BEACON, REVEAL and Embolden did not render readable study details; sponsor documents supplied the cited protocol information.
The full TANGELO article text was unavailable from the publisher preview and the Erasmus University repository download.
No position rejecting post-symptomatic restoration as a goal was identified in the Angelman and Rett roadmaps or the gene-therapy society's Angelman guidance.

definition = "After symptoms appear, treatment restores UBE3A function in neurons in Angelman syndrome or MECP2 function in neurons in Rett syndrome, enabling a person to acquire or regain developmental skills. Approaches include supplying a functional copy of the affected gene and, in Angelman syndrome, turning on the normally silent UBE3A copy inherited from the father.". Reason: The definition needs to pair each syndrome with its gene and explain what reactivating an existing copy means in Angelman syndrome.

goal.need = "In Angelman syndrome, the estimated chance of brushing teeth with help by age 15 was 13% with a class I deletion and 85% with a pathogenic UBE3A variant. Among 1,228 females with classic Rett syndrome, fewer than 6.3% of eligible participants gained or regained any of 51 skills per year after age six. Therapies teach skills and medicines ease symptoms, but the protein deficiency persists. Gaining hand use or communication after symptoms appear could reduce dependence in daily life. Recovery may vary by skill, as it does in Angelman mouse models.". Reason: The current text gives the size of the Angelman cohort without showing what the genotype difference means for daily care.

add statement by Rett Syndrome Research Trust, 2017: "the delivery of healthy copies of the MECP2 gene to compensate for the mutated copy". Reason: The 2017 roadmap documents a patient research foundation setting MECP2 restoration as a goal before the current commercial programme.

edit completion: basis = "FDA determines safety and effectiveness for the proposed indication. The Atlas requires evidence that gene restoration enables patients with established symptoms to acquire or regain developmental abilities. For example, FDA approved trofinetide for Rett syndrome on caregiver symptom ratings and clinician ratings of overall improvement at 12 weeks. That approval establishes a different benefit. Developmental gains apply to the population and follow-up studied."; refs = [3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 21]. Reason: The basis can explain the clinical distinction using an actual FDA approval and identify who selected the developmental-benefit requirement.

edit m1: title = "Gene restoration produces the expected biological response in an animal with established disease signs."; criterion = "A relevant animal model shows signs of the disorder before gene restoration. After intervention, the model shows a biological response consistent with the response expected in humans."; set_by = "FDA, Human Gene Therapy for Rare Diseases, section IV, recommends the model-response test for gene-therapy products. The post-onset condition defines the scope of this entry."; set_by_kind = "regulator"; threshold_quote = "should demonstrate a biological response to the investigational GT product that is similar to the expected response in humans."; threshold_ref = 6; refs = [6, 9, 10]. Reason: The current animal criterion can be met before symptoms appear and includes two historical outcomes inside the test.

edit m2: criterion = "At least one participant with established symptoms receives the investigational UBE3A- or MECP2-restoring treatment under an early-phase clinical protocol."; set_by = "FDA, 21 CFR 312.21(a), defines initial human administration. TANGELO and the early REVEAL cohorts apply this stage to the two syndromes."; set_by_kind = "regulator"; threshold_quote = "initial introduction of an investigational new drug into humans."; threshold_ref = 14; refs = [14, 11, 12, 13, 8]. Reason: The early-phase dosing test currently includes later safety and developmental findings that are unnecessary to establish administration.

add milestone after m2: "An early clinical study finds preliminary evidence of improved developmental function.". Reason: Preliminary evidence of developmental benefit is a distinct result between first dosing and pivotal testing.

edit m3: criterion = "At least one symptomatic participant receives the gene-restoring treatment in the pivotal cohort of a study designed to evaluate efficacy and safety for a marketing application. In a multiphase protocol, the qualifying dose must be given in the pivotal part."; threshold_quote = "Phase 3 studies are expanded controlled and uncontrolled trials."; threshold_ref = 14; refs = [14, 7, 13, 8]. Reason: The pivotal-entry criterion mixes the first qualifying dose with enrolment totals and needs to identify the pivotal cohort in multiphase trials.

edit m4: criterion = "Meet the trial's prespecified primary developmental endpoint. In Rett syndrome at 12 months, Embolden requires at least 9 of 25 participants both to gain at least one of 28 milestones and to score 3 or better on the Clinical Global Impression of Improvement. TSHA-102 REVEAL requires at least 33% to gain or regain at least one of 28 milestones. In Angelman syndrome, BEACON compares change in Bayley-4 raw cognition or expressive communication with sham at week 56 in ages 1\u201317. Obudanersen REVEAL compares change in raw expressive communication without caregiver input with placebo at week 52 in its paediatric cohort. ASPIRE compares change in raw cognition with sham at week 48."; set_by = "The Embolden and TSHA-102 REVEAL protocols define separate Rett responder thresholds. Oak Hill Bio, Ionis and Ultragenyx define the Angelman endpoints for BEACON, obudanersen REVEAL and ASPIRE respectively. The quoted threshold is specific to TSHA-102 REVEAL."; set_by_kind = "protocol"; threshold_quote = "A response rate of 33% is the minimum threshold for success sufficient to reject the natural history established null hypothesis of 6.7%"; threshold_ref = 13; refs = [13, 25, 8, 7, 26, 15, 16]. Reason: The criterion omits both trials named REVEAL and reports the ASPIRE outcome where its prespecified test belongs.

add milestone after m4: "FDA accepts a marketing application for a gene-restoring treatment for substantive review.". Reason: FDA acceptance of a marketing application for review is an observable stage between pivotal evidence and an approval decision.
